To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cerebral atrophy occurs in early stages of MS and progresses three times quicker than in healthy individuals; GM atrophy is more pronounced than WM loss, and has a different pattern of regional distribution in different clinical phenotyes; deep GM atrophy is correlated with WM lesion as with cortical atrophy; GM atrophy correlates with T2 lesion load, clinical impairment and cognitive dysfunction.
MS is characterized by a complex pattern of atrophy, which is more extensive in the brain than in the spinal cord, and is correlated with the clinical phenotype, disability, and cognitive function.
MS is characterized by atrophy of GM and WM in all brain areas, and this atrophy is more pronounced in the progressive disease course.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the atrophy in MS using MRI-morphometric techniques.
the study of cerebral atrophy in MS patients, with the use of MRI morphometry methods.
the study of atrophy in different clinical phenotypes of MS and its correlations with clinical and MRI parameters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MS is a neurodegenerative disease of both the white and gray matter.
MS is not a demyelination disease only, but a neurodegenerative process as well.
MS is a neurodegenerative disease, with a progressive course, which starts at the earliest stages of the disease, and is more pronounced in patients with progressive disease phenotypes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MS patients with more severe atrophy and more extensive WM lesions are at a higher risk of progression.
MRI-morphometry could be used as a sensitive and reliable measure to assess the neurodegenerativ component of MS.
MS is a neurodegenerative disease, which is characterized by a progressive loss of GM and WM.
The main takeaway from our work is that

MRI-morphometry is a promising tool for the evaluation of neurodegeneration in MS, which may help to identify patients at risk of progression and to develop new therapies for the treatment of neurodegeneration and its consequences.
cerebral atrophy is a common feature of MS and can be used as a marker for disease progression and disability.
the MRI-morphometry is a promising tool for the assessment of the neurodegeneratve component of MS.
